question: What % of people in Ireland aged 3 and over say they can speak Irish?
nugget: 1.87 million people say they can speak Irish. But only 71,968 use it every day outside school or college. That’s fewer people than a full Croke Park.

question: What % of people living in Ireland were born outside Ireland?
nugget: One in five people living here was born abroad. Ten times as many people speak a language other than English or Irish at home (751,507) as speak Irish daily outside school.

question: What % of primary school children in Ireland go to school by car?
nugget: More than half of primary kids are driven to school. The good news: 88% more primary pupils cycled to school than in 2016.

question: What % of people in Ireland smoke, either daily or occasionally?
nugget: Nearly 450,000 people still smoke every day. And it shows: over 90% of never-smokers rate their health good or very good, against 79% of daily smokers.

question: What % of 25–34-year-olds in Ireland have a third-level qualification?
nugget: Ireland’s young adults are the most educated in the EU. Ireland has nearly three times Romania’s rate (23%) and beats the EU’s 2030 target of 45% by a mile.

question: What % of people in Ireland identify as Roman Catholic?
nugget: In 2016 it was 79%. That’s ten points gone in just six years.

question: What % of households in Ireland have solar panels?
nugget: Only 6% of all homes have solar panels. But among homes built since 2016, it’s about 30%. New Ireland is going solar.

question: What % of people aged 15 and over in Ireland are married?
nugget: Single is catching up: 43% of adults are single, up from 41% in 2016, while married slipped from 48% to 46%.

question: What % of people in Ireland say their health is good or very good?
nugget: That’s down from 87% in 2016. The biggest slide was in people aged 35 to 39: only 52% said “very good”, down from 61%.

question: Mayo has the highest rate in the country. What % of people in Mayo are unpaid carers?
nugget: Ireland now has over 299,000 unpaid carers, up 53% in six years. Dublin City has the lowest rate, at 5%.

question: What % of occupied homes in Ireland are lived in by their owners?
nugget: Eleven years earlier it was almost 70%. Homes rented from private landlords have climbed to 330,632, up 7% since 2016.

question: What % of people living in Ireland are not Irish citizens?
nugget: Dual Irish citizenship is booming: 170,597 people hold it, up 63% in six years.

question: What % of people in Ireland have a long-lasting condition or difficulty?
nugget: That’s more than 1.1 million people, more than one in five. For 407,342 of them, it affects their life to a great extent or a lot.

question: Of people in Ireland who’ve finished full-time education, what % have at least an ordinary degree?
nugget: In 2011 it was 25%. That’s nine points in eleven years.

question: What % of people aged 15 and over in Ireland are in the labour force (working or looking for work)?
nugget: Men 67%, women 56%. Women’s participation is rising (55% in 2016) while men’s has dipped (from 68%).
